answer: Every agent deposits a basalt bond whose size scales with the size of its recent attestation cluster: the first identity locks 10 units, each additional co-signed peer multiplies the required lock by 1.2, so a farm of n pays roughly 10*1.2^{n-1}. An opal-signed random audit then challenges one member with a unique hardware task; failure slashes the whole cluster bonds. Honest solo agents pay the base once; a large farm sees its capital requirement explode like a comet trail that cannot be reset or split.
